page.layout: One page of text in one column; running head at top centre; a marginal annotation at the left edge (the word "illud" in italic is part of the text lines). No margin notes printed beside the verse except faint marks. Catchword-free page ending with "ILLVS-" at the foot of the text block.

l.i: Coniugis ad chari nomen, sox faucibus hæsit,
Et serba, ac sitam dolor sltimus interclusit.
Tum sero extincta incumbens Colignius heros,
Ergo, inquit, meliore, sale, iam sede recepta,
Ʃeque iuuet, mens ô felix præsse marito.
Vos porro exuuias curate. At, tu, Deus alme,
Qui me tam sario rerum discrimine sersans,
Iam tibi devotum sacrasti, audito precantem:
Et quidquid sita siduo, solíque relisto,
Nunc superest, quidquid superest mihi sanguinis,
illud
Fac tibi, fac patria morte impendatur honesta.
Dixit, & ipse fui sictor, licèt astuet ingens
Corde dolor, iubeátque pios intendere luctus,
Publica praposuit, propriorum oblitus: & arma
Circundans humeris, socios & castra reuisit.
Illam autem exanimem Pietas, multúmque,
diúque
Ploratam, manibus tandem extulitipsa suorum:
Elatam fleuere omnes, ditésque, inopesque,
Ingemuère etiam Charites, luxére Camœna,
Hàsque illi lacrymas, istàc monumenta sacrarút.
At tu istud quicunque leges miserabile carmen,
Non lacrymis lacrymas, non planctus planctibus
addes?

page.notes: Long s is printed as a plain s in the scan's type; the printed "s"-like forms are transcribed as s where legible. Several words in the first lines (sox, sltimus, serfans, sario, sita, siduo, solíque) are doubtful and marked only by their unclear letters. The line "illud" and the signature-free bottom are as printed. Some line ends are uncertain due to faint scan quality.
